newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine allows banks to seize debtors' forex a/cs.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine allows banks to seize debtors' forex a/cs.

text.p: A new order from Ukraine's central bank allows commercial banks to seize money from the hard currency accounts of debtor enterprises.
The new order, circulated by e-mail to commercial banks, is effective as of October 20.

Many Ukrainian enterprises owe hryvnia to various creditors like the tax inspection department, energy companies, workers, and other enterprises for goods and services. But some deposit money in hard currency accounts and claim they do not have hryvnia accounts to pay the debts, officials say.
The order states its goal as "speeding up resolution of the debt crisis, and regulating relations between official bodies and legal entities."
Government figures say that only half of forecast budget revenues have been received so far this year.
The order said enterprises will be given five days following notification of claim by courts, to repay the debt.

The bank is required to notify the enterprise of a claim against it within one day of receiving the claim, and if the debt is not paid within five days, must convert foreign currency to hryvnia to clear the debt.
Debts to foreign creditors will remain in hard currency, the order said. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
